He also contributed the Turing test to philosophy of artificial intelligence and the Turing pattern concept to mathematical and theoretical biology.
Born in London and raised in southern England, Turing graduated from King's College, Cambridge, and earned a doctorate from Princeton University in 1938.
During World War II, he worked at the Government Code and Cypher School at Bletchley Park, Britain's codebreaking centre, and focused on decrypting German naval messages as the head of Hut 8.

Bartholomew's Church on Clyde Road in Ballsbridge, Dublin.[20] Julius's work with the ICS brought the family to British India, where his grandfather had been a general in the Bengal Army.
However, both Julius and Ethel wanted their children to be brought up in Britain, so they moved to Maida Vale,[21] London, where Alan Turing was born on 23 June 1912, as recorded by a blue plaque on the outside of the nursing home where he was born,[22][23] which later became the Colonnade Hotel.[17][24] Turing had an elder brother, John Ferrier Turing, father of Dermot Turing, 12th Baronet of the Turing baronets.[25] In 1922, he discovered Natural Wonders Every Child Should Know by Edwin Tenney Brewster.
He credited it with opening his eyes to science.[26] Turing's father's civil service commission was still active during Turing's childhood years, and his parents travelled between Hastings in the United Kingdom[27] and India, leaving their two sons to stay with a retired Army couple.
